cases.exposure_context_quote: A 35-year-old female weighing 60 kg present to the emergency department with an alleged history of deliberate ingestion of 50 ml of 50% fipronil liquid solution (~ 417.6 mg/kg).
cases.agent_quote: deliberate ingestion of 50 ml of 50% fipronil liquid solution (~ 417.6 mg/kg)
cases.circumstance: Deliberate ingestion 3 h prior to presentation following a domestic argument; family provided the container for confirmation.

symptoms.finding: 3 episodes of vomiting of foul-smelling liquid matter within first 2 h after ingestion
symptoms.quote: Within the first 2 h after the ingestion, she had 3 episodes of vomiting of foul-smelling liquid matter, and epigastric pain.
Within the first 2 h after the ingestion, she had 3 episodes of vomiting of foul-smelling liquid matter, and epigastric pain.

symptoms.finding: no seizures, skin irritation, or neurologic deficit; GCS 15/15 with mid-sized reactive pupils
symptoms.quote: On examination, she was conscious, pulse rate was 96 regular, blood pressure 110/70, and 98% oxygen saturation. Neurologic examination revealed a Glasgow coma scale score of 15/15, with mid-sized and reactive pupils.

labs.name: hemogram, liver function, renal function, electrolytes
labs.quote: The patient’s hemogram, liver function, renal function and electrolytes were all in normal limits.

labs.name: toxicology screen / blood fipronil or fipronil sulphone levels / 12-lead ECG
labs.quote: A toxicology screen panel, blood fipronil or fipronil sulphone levels, and 12 led ECG was not available.

treatment.name: proton pump inhibitor; monitoring for seizure; psychiatric counselling; supportive management
treatment.quote: She was treated with proton pump inhibitor and was monitored for seizure throughout her hospitalization. Psychiatric counselling was obtained.

treatment.name: no gastrointestinal decontamination (activated charcoal unavailable; gastric lavage not performed)
treatment.quote: Given the limited data regarding gastric lavage for fipronil poisoning and the unavailability of activated charcoal, gastrointestinal decontamination was not performed.

cases.icu_admission: no (observed in hospital; ICU admission not mentioned)
cases.outcome: survived; discharged after 48 h of observation in stable condition with favourable outcome; remained asymptomatic during follow-up at nearby health centre
cases.outcome_quote: Following 48 h of observation, she was discharged in stable condition with favourable outcome. ... She continued her remote follow up at nearby health centre and remained asymptomatic during follow up.
cases.notes: Diagnosis based on clinical presentation and history, confirmed by family-provided container/photograph; vomiting may have reduced toxin available for absorption.
